newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian coffee arrivals approach 300,000 tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian coffee arrivals approach 300,000 tonnes.

text.p: Arrivals of 1996/97 (Oct-Sept) coffee at Ivorian ports totalled around 290-295,000 tonnes by June 13, up from last year's total of 180,000 tonnes, port sources said on Friday.
Arrivals by May 25 had been 265,000 tonnes, about 105,000 tonnes up on the same period in 1995/96.
Port sources said exports had begun to pick up after a sluggish start to the season, with quality problems slowing grading.
Official port data put cumulative bean exports to the end of March at 45,783 tonnes, against 58,667 at the same stage a year earlier.
April export data showed a further 21,545 tonnes of beans shipped from the main port of Abidjan.
San Pedro port data for April have been delayed by communications problems.
May statistics for both ports, including exports of coffee products, are expected to be ready in late June.
Local roasters account for around 30,000 tonnes of Ivorian beans a year.
